Hi Aisha / Samir —

Thanks for the time today — good convo. Quick recap + asks so we can size the right autoscale profile and warm-pool recommendation: 

1) Target SLOs you called out: p95 end-to-end latency for streaming responses <= 300ms (for most flows), p99 <= 1s for heavy multi-token completions.
2) Traffic/throughput: baseline ~1,200 requests/minute, typical concurrency ~50, expected peak bursts up to ~300 concurrent requests (bursts last ~3–7 minutes).
3) Streaming: yes — token-level streaming is required for product UX on chat flows.
4) Tolerance: you prefer errors/queueing over long cold-start delays; graceful degradation acceptable (smaller-model fallback) but want preserved streaming where possible.

Next steps from our side: 1) confirm any missing traffic patterns (burst cadence, daily window), 2) share a short RFI + our autoscale/warm-pool proposal, and 3) schedule a technical deep-dive with engineering to validate scale-up times and queueing behavior.

- Latency targets: p95 <= 300ms is what product needs for chat UX. For longer generative flows we can tolerate p99 up to 1s as you noted.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline concurrency ~50, typical steady throughput 1,200 rpm. Spikes are unpredictable but we modeled a marketing-triggered spike that jumps to ~300 concurrent for 3–5 minutes. We also see smaller spikes (~120–150) several times per day.

Subject: Re: Autoscale SLO & burst capacity follow-up — engineering notes

Hi Marissa / Aisha —

Thanks for the clear ask. I ran the simulation data and summarized below; high-level guidance and conservative numbers included so FastPay can design against worst-case.

1) Cold start (no warm pool): full scale-up from cold GPUs (node allocation + model load) to be ready for steady token generation is ~90–150 seconds depending on model size and region. During this period we can accept requests into the front-end queue but streaming will be delayed until the model surfaces — initial token emission could be delayed by the full cold-start window for requests that hit a cold node.

2) Warm pool behavior: with pre-warmed instances (model loaded, KV cache primed for typical sequence lengths) per-node readiness is ~8–18 seconds to start serving new requests (depends on instance type and quantization). Our recommended minimum warm pool to cover an initial spike to 300 concurrent: 5 pre-warmed nodes (assumes each node can sustain ~60 effective concurrent streaming sessions with our streaming-optimized runtime and batching). This gives initial headroom to avoid cold loads while autoscaler brings additional nodes up.

3) Autoscaler fill time: with warm pool + rapid provisioning we see incremental node add times of ~15–30s per additional node (allocation + final readiness). So with the 5-node warm pool you can expect first-wave coverage in ~10–20s and full scale to peak in ~40–70s depending on how aggressively the autoscaler policy ramps.

4) Queueing/backpressure: front-end queueing is configurable. We recommend queue depth of 2,000 requests with a per-request timeout at the customer level (e.g., 30s). If the queue fills we support two options: (a) overflow 429s for non-critical routes, or (b) route to a smaller but warm fallback model (lower-cost) that preserves streaming but with lower-quality outputs. For FastPay's profile (prefer queueing over repeated cold delays) we'd set a larger queue and route to fallback only when queue > 1,500.

5) Streaming during scale-up: streaming can be preserved for requests that are assigned to warm nodes. Requests that hit cold nodes will see delayed first tokens until the model is ready. To mitigate: (a) keep a minimal warm pool sized as above; (b) use short-lived pre-warm schedules around known marketing events (automated schedules via our console); (c) enable early-token proxies for some prompt types — we can stream partial tokens from a tiny local microservice while model warms, but that requires product acceptance and quality checks.

6) Cost tradeoffs: keeping a 5-node warm pool for a 3-month campaign will add steady-state cost (approx estimate in attached autoscale-sim-results.csv). We'll follow up with a conservative monthly run-rate.

Proposed next steps:
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive to validate exact numbers with FastPay's traffic traces (we can use the RFI spreadsheet you sent).
- I'll prepare a short doc that maps warm-pool sizes to expected p95/p99 latency under the customer's real trace and share an updated cost delta.

Happy to jump on a call tomorrow afternoon PST — Marissa can coordinate.

Thanks,
